claims.text: The starting feedstock is homogeneous gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle size of 10–60 μm dispersed in an acrylate-based photocurable resin.
Replacing ambient-air debinding with continuous mechanical-pump evacuation will improve dimensional precision.
Replacing ambient-air debinding with continuous mechanical-pump evacuation will improve mechanical integrity.
An oxygen-deficient debinding environment minimizes oxidation-induced pore formation and cracking.
Reduced oxidation enables stronger interparticle bonding and densification at lower sintering temperatures.
The proposed debinding schedule uses 1 h holds at 300 °C and 450 °C, followed by heating to 500 °C under continuous mechanical-pump evacuation.
The proposed specimens are sintered for 24 h at temperatures between 800 and 1100 °C.
Oxygen-deficient debinding retains residual carbon in regions formerly occupied by resin.
Residual carbon retained after oxygen-deficient debinding reduces gas evolution and pore volume.
Oxygen-deficient debinding limits oxide-layer formation on particle surfaces.
Reduced pore volume and surface oxidation reduce surface cracking and preserve interparticle contact.
In an oxygen-rich environment, rapid oxidation of the resin and powder generates CO and CO2.
CO and CO2 generated during oxygen-rich debinding induce pressure-driven cracking.
Surface oxides formed during oxygen-rich processing hinder particle interdiffusion.
Oxygen-deficient specimens will densify at a sintering temperature approximately 50 °C lower than oxygen-rich specimens.
Oxygen-deficient specimens will have reduced surface cracking and porosity relative to oxygen-rich specimens.
Oxygen-deficient specimens will have compressive strength comparable to or greater than approximately 5.1 MPa.
Oxygen-rich AlCrFeNiSi specimens require sintering at 1100 °C for full consolidation.
Oxygen-rich AlCrFeNiSi specimens sintered at 1100 °C have approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength.
Oxygen-rich baseline specimens exhibit noticeable surface cracking and a porous microstructure.
